attacks.claim: The mandated public announcement says text alerts are for every cardholder, but juvenile cards do not see the SMS option; only a guardian can opt in, using their own number. The copy is fixed 'exactly' and goes to the site, posters and newsletter, so it misstates who can use the feature. The fix is one line, so correct it before it crosses.
attacks.evidence: "Text alerts for holds, for every cardholder." vs. "juvenile cards do not show it"

attacks.claim: Assistive-technology testing covers only the web opt-in form. The locker touchscreen has audio guidance and a high-contrast mode, but only vendor and staff acceptance testing is cited, with no AT or blind-user check and no tactile keypad described. The service-desk fallback limits the harm to out-of-hours pickup.
attacks.evidence: "Opt-in form with NVDA + Firefox, VoiceOver iOS" vs. "audio guidance through a headphone jack"

attacks.claim: The locker rollback remaps holds to the desk but does not say whether outstanding single-use codes or the physical cells are disabled.
Batched messages show one locker, code and date. The artifact does not say how holds at different locations or with different deadlines are handled.
attacks.evidence: "extra holds are batched into one message"
